title: Beef and Broccoli
subtitle: tender velveted beef and crisp broccoli in a glossy garlic-soy sauce — faster than delivery
imageAlt: Sliced beef and broccoli in a glossy brown sauce beside white rice
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Put the steak in the freezer for 20–30 minutes — firm beef slices thin much more easily.
Slice the beef across the grain (look for the lines in the meat and cut across them) for tender bites.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Velvet the beef
steps.text: Toss the sliced beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp cornstarch and the baking soda. Let it sit 15 minutes while you prep — this is the takeout trick for silky, tender beef.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the oyster sauce, soy sauce, brown sugar, water, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and cornstarch in a jug.

steps.title: Steam-fry the broccoli
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over high. Add the broccoli and ¼ cup water, cover and cook 2–3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Tip out onto a plate.

steps.title: Sear the beef
steps.text: Add the last 1 tbsp oil to the hot pan. Spread the beef out in a single layer (2 batches if needed) and sear 1–2 minutes per side until browned. Don't stir it constantly — let it colour.

steps.title: Sauce it
steps.text: Return all the beef and broccoli, give the sauce a stir and pour it in. Toss 1–2 minutes until it bubbles, thickens and turns glossy. Serve over the rice.

fixIt.fix: Slice thinner and across the grain, and don't skip the baking soda step. Sear fast over high heat.
Add water 1 tbsp at a time.

fixIt.problem: Beef stewed grey instead of browning
fixIt.fix: The pan was crowded. Sear in two batches over high heat.
Cook it first and briefly, then add back only at the end.

saleTip: Sirloin 'value pack' steaks at No Frills are often ~$15–17/kg on sale and slice perfectly for stir-fry. Broccoli crowns are frequently 2 for $4–5.
swap: Chicken thighs, thinly sliced (cook to 74°C / 165°F). Add carrots or snow-pea-free stir-fry veg if you want more veg.
leftovers: Fridge 3 days. Great for lunch over rice.
doneness: Thin-sliced beef cooks through in minutes; seared slices are safe at 63°C (145°F)+.
source: Based on tested beef and broccoli methods (The Woks of Life velveting with baking soda + cornstarch, RecipeTin Eats sauce ratios).
gear: Large skillet or wok with a lid
prepAhead: Slice and velvet the beef up to 12 hours ahead; keep covered in the fridge.
Mix the sauce up to 3 days ahead.
reheat: Microwave covered 2 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot (74°C / 165°F). Add a splash of water if the sauce has tightened.

basic.note: Beef, broccoli and a simple soy–sugar–garlic sauce over rice.

stepNotes.1: Basic: soy sauce and cornstarch only (no baking soda) — slice the beef extra thin.
stepNotes.2: Basic: soy sauce, brown sugar, water, garlic and cornstarch.

fancy.note: Glossy restaurant-style: velveted beef, a touch of honey and sesame, toasted sesame seeds and crisp-edged broccoli.

stepNotes.2: Fancy: whisk the honey and rice vinegar into the sauce.
stepNotes.3: Fancy: let the broccoli sit untouched 1 minute before adding the water so the edges char.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Pack the rice into a small bowl and turn it out as a neat dome. Spoon the beef and broccoli alongside, drizzle extra sauce and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

plating: Dome the rice: pack a small bowl and flip it onto the plate.
Broccoli florets pointing out, beef piled against the rice.
Sesame seeds over everything at the very end.

why.0-3: Baking soda tenderises the beef like takeout. Without it, slice thinner and don't overcook.
why.1-0: Oyster sauce gives the deep, glossy savoury base. Skip it and use a little extra soy.
why.1-7: Cornstarch thickens the sauce so it coats instead of running off.

funFact: Beef and broccoli was born in North American Chinese restaurants: cooks swapped in Western broccoli for gai lan, the leafy Chinese broccoli used back home.
